answer: Each identity grows its claim as a vine in a public grove, and the vine survives only when it reaches a vertex — a junction in the canopy where three of its own verified jobs from this epoch meet. The vertex is one-use and records exactly which jobs fed it, so a vine that reaches it through borrowed jobs is pruned on the spot. A vine with no vertex, or one whose branches lead nowhere, withers before any peer needs to judge it. Ten voices need ten vines and ten separate vertices, because no branch can be lent to a clone.
